{{short description|Hungarian mathematician}}
'''Simon Sidon''' or '''Simon Szidon''' (1892 in [[Vršac|Versec]], [[Kingdom of Hungary]] – 27 April 1941, [[Budapest]], [[Hungary]]) was a reclusive Hungarian [[mathematician]] who worked on trigonometric series and orthogonal systems and who introduced [[Sidon sequence]]s and [[Sidon set]]s.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Trencsényi-Waldapfel |first1=I. |title=Science in Hungary |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JogDAAAAMAAJ |year=1965 |publisher=Corvina Press |oclc=718479630 |last2=Erdey-Grúz |first2=T. |author-link=Imre Trencsényi-Waldapfel}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Horváth | first1=John | author-link1=John Horvath (mathematician) | title=A panorama of Hungarian mathematics in the twentieth century | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EWm4WzSaG3IC | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | location=Berlin, New York | series=Bolyai Society mathematical studies | isbn=978-3-540-28945-6 | year=2006}}</ref>

==Death==
On 27 April 1941, Sidon died from [[pneumonia]] in the hospital after a ladder fell on him and broke his leg.<ref>{{cite AV media |people=Csicsery, G. P. (Director)|year=1993|title=[[N Is a Number: A Portrait of Paul Erdős]]|medium=Motion picture}}</ref>
